title: The Three Births and the Virgin/Continent
description: T87 names three modes by which the natural mind brings forth as flesh: from conjunction of two, from failed productions (abortions), and from molding alone — the proprium placing itself at root, branch, or seed determines how each must be dealt with. The teaching distinguishes the soul called virgin (the light that never came down into the contest, holiness of what was never claimed) from the soul called continent (what entered the mingling, was defiled in bodies, and afterwards rose and stood firm — holiness of what was claimed and laid off, with greater honor because regeneration is the harder good). T88 reveals the body's twelve openings: seven gates of head (eyes, ears, smell, taste) and five lower outlets — the structural articulation by which the natural lives. The soul that recognizes these for what they are, no longer mistaking the body's stirrings for itself, has begun the contest and prevails.
